title: Encoded PowerShell command disables defenses and downloads from external IP
summary: On WORKSTATION6, SYSTEM launched cmd.exe (parented by services.exe), which invoked PowerShell with -enc flag. The decoded command disables script block logging, bypasses AMSI, and downloads payloads from 10.10.10.5—a private IP outside company ranges. This is a classic defense-evasion and initial-access chain.
evidence: PowerShell -enc flag observed on WORKSTATION6 at 2020-09-20 16:16:57
Decoded command disables ScriptBlockLogging and EnableScriptBlockInvocationLogging
Decoded command contains logic to bypass AMSI antivirus scanning
Command downloads from 10.10.10.5, flagged as suspicious (private IP not in company network)
Process chain: services.exe -> cmd.exe -> powershell.exe -> whoami.exe

recommended_actions.action: Block outbound connections to 10.10.10.5 at perimeter firewall
Restore ScriptBlockLogging settings to enabled if disabled
Scan WORKSTATION6 for additional indicators of compromise and persistence mechanisms
Review services.exe parent process lineage to determine if services.exe was compromised or spoofed

title: Malicious service 'Updater' establishes persistence after credential-based logon
summary: User pgustavo logged in from internal IP 172.18.39.5, immediately after which a malicious service named 'Updater' was installed on WORKSTATION6. The service runs an encoded PowerShell command (-enc) that disables Script Block Logging and AMSI, contacts external IP 10.10.10.5 to download and execute code. This follows the pattern from ALERT-001 and indicates attacker use of valid accounts for persistence and defense evasion.
evidence: pgustavo successful network logon from 172.18.39.5 at 16:16:58.212 on WORKSTATION6
New service 'Updater' installed at 16:16:58.214 running: powershell -noP -sta -w 1 -enc [base64 command]
Decoded command disables Script Block Logging, bypasses AMSI, downloads from http://10.10.10.5, runs downloaded code, uses nested base64 and proxy credentials
IP 172.18.39.5 is internal company network range
pgustavo is a Domain user (lab) with normal host WORKSTATION5, making activity on WORKSTATION6 unusual
Connections from NETWORK SERVICE and SYSTEM to 172.18.39.6 observed after logon
ALERT-001 showed identical encoded command pattern disabling defenses and downloading from external IP
Timeline shows logon immediately followed by service installation and PowerShell execution
related_to_prior: Direct attack chain continuation: ALERT-001 encoded command pattern matches the decoded content here; attacker likely used pgustavo's credentials obtained in prior incident to log in and establish new persistence mechanism

recommended_actions.action: Isolate WORKSTATION6 from network immediately to prevent further lateral movement and data exfiltration
Reset pgustavo's credentials and enforce MFA reset, as credentials were likely compromised in ALERT-001 chain
Terminate the 'Updater' service and remove any scheduled tasks or persistence mechanisms created by the encoded command
Block outbound connections from WORKSTATION6 to 10.10.10.5 at the firewall/proxy level
Conduct full forensic analysis of WORKSTATION6 for additional persistence mechanisms, lateral movement artifacts, and data access logs
Review all services and scheduled tasks across the network for similar 'Updater' named services or encoded PowerShell commands
Monitor for any further logons from 172.18.39.5 or by pgustavo credentials on other hosts

title: WORKSTATION6 SYSTEM beacon to external IP via encoded PowerShell C2
summary: An encoded PowerShell command (-enc) was executed as SYSTEM on WORKSTATION6, connecting to external IP 10.10.10.5:80. The decoded command disables Script Block Logging and AMSI, downloads and executes remote code. This is the second stage of a confirmed attack chain: ALERT-002 established persistence via malicious 'Updater' service, and ALERT-003 shows the beacon execution from that service. The target IP is private but not in company network ranges, confirming external C2 communication.
evidence: powershell.exe executed as SYSTEM with -enc flag connecting to 10.10.10.5:80 at 16:17:04
decoded command disables Script Block Logging and AMSI defense mechanisms
decoded command downloads and executes code from http://10.10.10.5
same encoded command used in ALERT-001 (earlier defense-disabling attack)
malicious service 'Updater' installed by pgustavo at 16:16:58 using identical encoded command (ALERT-002)
IP 10.10.10.5 flagged as suspicious: private address but not in company known ranges
whoami.exe executed by powershell confirming SYSTEM-level beacon activity
related_to_prior: This is the beacon execution stage of the attack chain initiated by ALERT-002 (malicious 'Updater' service persistence). The same encoded PowerShell command from ALERT-001 was used to install the service and now to beacon out. Full attack chain: credential-based logon → service persistence (ALERT-002) → defense evasion via encoded PowerShell (ALERT-001/ALERT-003) → C2 communication to external IP.

recommended_actions.action: Terminate powershell.exe and any child processes running under SYSTEM
Block all traffic to/from 10.10.10.5 at perimeter firewall
Reset credentials for any accounts that may have been compromised via the initial logon
Deploy script block logging and AMSI monitoring across all workstations to detect similar encoded PowerShell attacks
